| Web Search Results |  | In Next.js, Server Actions are asynchronous functions executed on the server to handle tasks like form submissions and data mutations. The placement of these functions depends on whether you're working with Server Components or Client Components.<br/><br/>**For Server Components:**<br/><br/>- **Inline Definition:** You can define Server Actions directly within the component by adding the `'use server'` directive at the beginning of the function.<br/><br/>  <br/>```javascript<br/>  // Server Component<br/>  export default function Page() \{<br/>    // Server Action<br/>    async function create() \{<br/>      'use server';<br/>      // ...<br/>    \}<br/><br/>    return (<br/>      // ...<br/>    );<br/>  \}<br/>  ```<br/><br/><br/>  ([nextjs.org](https://nextjs.org/docs/14/app/building-your-application/data-fetching/server-actions-and-mutations?utm_source=openai))<br/><br/>- **Module-Level Definition:** Alternatively, place the `'use server'` directive at the top of a separate file to mark all its exports as Server Actions.<br/><br/>  <br/>```javascript<br/>  // app/actions.js<br/>  'use server';<br/><br/>  export async function create() \{<br/>    // ...<br/>  \}<br/>  ```<br/><br/><br/>  ([nextjs.org](https://nextjs.org/docs/14/app/building-your-application/data-fetching/server-actions-and-mutations?utm_source=openai))<br/><br/>**For Client Components:**<br/><br/>Client Components can only import Server Actions from files where the `'use server'` directive is applied at the module level. This approach ensures that the Server Actions are accessible to Client Components.<br/><br/><br/>```javascript<br/>// app/actions.js<br/>'use server';<br/><br/>export async function create() \{<br/>  // ...<br/>\}<br/>```<br/><br/><br/><br/>```javascript<br/>// app/ui/button.js<br/>import \{ create \} from '@/app/actions';<br/><br/>export function Button() \{<br/>  return (<br/>    // ...<br/>  );<br/>\}<br/>```<br/><br/><br/>([nextjs.org](https://nextjs.org/docs/14/app/building-your-application/data-fetching/server-actions-and-mutations?utm_source=openai))<br/><br/>**Organizing Server Actions:**<br/><br/>For better maintainability and reusability, especially in larger applications, it's advisable to organize Server Actions into dedicated files or directories. A common practice is to create a `server-actions` folder at the root level, alongside the `app` directory, to house these functions. This structure helps in keeping the codebase organized and makes it easier to manage server-side logic.<br/><br/>([github.com](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/55908?utm_source=openai))<br/><br/>By following these conventions, you can effectively manage Server Actions in your Next.js application, ensuring clear separation between server-side and client-side logic. |

## Current patterns in your codebase

1. **`lib/actions/`** — shared/general actions
   - Example: `lib/actions/auth.ts` (used across the app)

2. **Route-specific actions** — co-located with routes
   - Example: `app/(admin)/dashboard/projects/actions.ts`
   - Example: `app/(admin)/dashboard/skills/actions.ts`

## Best practices for file location

### Option 1: `lib/actions/` (recommended for shared actions)
```
lib/
  actions/
    auth.ts          ✅ (you already have this)
    projects.ts      (if shared across routes)
    users.ts
    ...
```
- Use for actions shared across multiple routes/components
- Easy to import from anywhere
- Clear separation of server logic

### Option 2: Co-located with routes (recommended for route-specific actions)
```
app/
  (admin)/
    dashboard/
      projects/
        actions.ts   ✅ (you already have this pattern)
        page.tsx
      skills/
        actions.ts   ✅
        page.tsx
```
- Use for actions specific to a route
- Keeps related code together
- Good for colocation

### Option 3: Root-level `actions/` directory
```
actions/
  projects.ts
  users.ts
  ...
```
- Alternative to `lib/actions/`
- Some teams prefer this for visibility

## Important requirements

1. Module-level `"use server"` directive at the top of the file:
   ```typescript
   "use server"
   
   export async function myAction() {
     // ...
   }
   ```

2. Client Components can only import from files with module-level `"use server"` (not inline actions)

3. Server Components can use inline actions or import from action files

## Recommendation

Your current structure is good:
- Keep shared actions in `lib/actions/`
- Keep route-specific actions co-located with their routes in `app/`

This balances reusability and colocation.
